references.text: God introduces himself with the same words: 'I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.'
God sends Moses to Israel to bring them out of Egypt, a pattern that is repeated when God sends a prophet to Israel in the time of the judges.
Joshua reminds the people that the Lord brought them out of Egypt and out of the house of slavery.
The Lord speaks through Samuel and reminds Israel that he brought them up from Egypt and delivered them from the hand of the Egyptians.
God sent prophets to the people to warn them and call them back, just as he sent a prophet to Israel in the time of the judges.
By a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet they were kept safe.
The Lord reminds the people that he brought them up from Egypt and freed them from the house of slavery.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord brought them out with a strong hand and delivered them from the house of slavery in Egypt.
The angel of the Lord reminds Israel that God brought them up from Egypt, a parallel to the prophet's message in Judges 6.
